caption: The drawing features a detailed illustration of an early phonograph or gramophone. The largest object is a black, cone-shaped horn on the right, which is attached to a mechanism built on a rectangular wooden base with a light brown color and visible grain. The horn is designed to amplify sound and is connected at its narrow end to a circular structure with mechanical parts and a metallic appearance. This structure is mounted on a metallic arm extending from the base. Below the arm are two black discs, each positioned atop separate supports and aligned horizontally. A system of belts or bands, colored brown or black, connects the two discs, giving the impression of transferring mechanical motion. Decorative gold details are visible on the supports. A small metallic or silver-colored plaque is affixed to the front edge of the wooden base. In the upper left corner of the drawing, there is an inset technical diagram in black and white; it shows a simpler outline of a similar mechanism labeled “RUBBER R,” likely intended to explain part of the device. The background of the drawing is off-white. In the bottom right corner, the text “U.S. Pat’d Nov. 8, 1887” is printed in black.
title: Gramophone
